MahaPAR · showing the form before and after

Five ways to put the current APAR form next to Form A draft v5. Click any snapshot to open it full size — that is the one thing a slide cannot do, and the reason this version exists alongside the deck.

1 · Page silhouettes 2 · Three stages, one view 3 · One stage at a time 4 · Page with callouts 5 · Structural stack

Option 1 · Page silhouettes

Every page of the current form against Form A, at the same scale. Deliberately unreadable: the eye reads area, not text.

Current · Form 1 · 11 pages
Form A · 2 pages
What this does well

The scale of the cut is unmistakable in one look, and nothing pretends to be legible. Works for the whole form, for either group.

What it cannot do

It says nothing about what changed inside the form.

Verdict: best for the whole-form view; pairs with a slide that explains the content.

Option 2 · All three stages in one view

On a slide this fails — nothing is readable. In HTML it works as a contact sheet: click any snapshot to open it full size.

Verdict: unusable on a slide, useful here as an index into the full snapshots.

Option 3 · One stage at a time, whole snapshot

The complete before and after for each stage, not a crop. This is the version that became three separate slides in the deck.

Current · Form 1, Section 2
→
Form A · Part 2
What the audience sees

The officer wrote free prose under open headings and repeated details the department already holds. Form A asks for targets against achievement, one significant contribution, and systemic factors — in set fields, with the officer's own details pre-filled.

Current · Form 1, Section 3 · 17 rated items
→
Form A · Part 3.1 · 7 dimensions
What the audience sees

Three tables of 17 rows, each graded by hand and averaged by hand, become one table of seven dimensions with written descriptors, and MahaPAR calculates the weighted overall grade.

Current · Form 1, Section 4B
→
Form A · Part 4
What the audience sees

The reviewing officer re-graded every dimension a second time. In Form A they record agreement or disagreement with the reporting officer's overall grade and their own overall grade, with reasons required only where they differ.

Verdict: the only option where the audience can actually read the change.

Option 4 · Full page with callout zooms

One page of the current form, with the two blocks that changed most marked and explained beside it.

Current · Form 1, page 6 of the form
Work completion · 3 items, graded and averaged by hand

In Form A this becomes dimensions 1 and 2, and MahaPAR does the arithmetic. Two of the three items collapse into ‘delivery of planned work’.

Personal attributes · 8 items

Overall bearing, emotional stability, moral courage and leadership are judged separately today. Form A folds them into two dimensions with written descriptors behind each.

The catch: the callouts carry the message, not the page. The page behind them is decoration, and a bilingual form needs each callout translated to be useful.

Verdict: familiar consulting device, but the page itself does no work.

Option 5 · Structural stack, no screenshot at all

Block height is proportional to the real length of each part, so the volume claim is made without asking anyone to read a form.
